app.name: Recito TTS
engine.elevenlabs.title: ElevenLabs
engine.elevenlabs.blurb: The most human-sounding voices. Paid per character, with 10,000 free credits a month.
engine.edge.title: Microsoft Edge voices
engine.edge.blurb: Natural voices from Microsoft. Free, needs an internet connection.
engine.piper.title: Piper
engine.piper.blurb: Starts instantly and always works. Sounds a bit more robotic.
engine.sapi.title: Windows voices
engine.sapi.blurb: The voices that come with Windows.
engine.mssp.title: MS Speech Platform
engine.mssp.blurb: ZiraPro, Hedda and friends through balcon under Wine.
engine.kokoro2.title: Kokoro
engine.kokoro2.blurb: Clear, natural voices that run on your own PC. Very quick, even without a graphics card.
engine.qwen3.title: Qwen3-TTS
engine.qwen3.blurb: Very natural and follows directions in plain words, like "calm, like an audiobook narrator".
engine.chatterbox.title: Chatterbox
engine.chatterbox.blurb: Expressive and lively. Can speak with a voice you record yourself.
engine.fish.title: Fish Audio S2 Pro
engine.fish.blurb: Strong emotions through tags like [whisper]. Needs a lot of graphics memory.
engine.fish.menu: Fish Audio S2 Pro (offline, graphics card)
engine.stepaudio.title: Step-Audio-EditX
engine.stepaudio.blurb: Emotion and style tags, mostly English. Heavy and slower.
cap.clone.tip: Voice cloning: record 10 to 15 seconds of someone speaking, and the model reads with that voice.
cap.tags.tip: Write little cues like [laugh] or [sigh] into the text, and the voice acts them out.
cap.instruct.tip: Describe how it should sound in plain words, for example "calm and warm".
cap.expr.tip: Set how lively or calm the voice sounds.
cap.style.tip: Tags change the emotion or speaking style of a sentence.
cap.markup.tip: Spell out how a tricky word is pronounced, like [Kokoro](/kˈOkəɹO/).
cap.fast.tip: The first words play almost instantly.
page.voice.title: Voice & engine
page.voice.text: Choose who reads to you. If an online voice is unreachable, the offline Piper voice steps in.
page.voice.offline: On this PC, no internet needed
voices.cloneHint: Speaks with any voice from a short recording. Create your own below; it shows up in both lists.
voices.instructHelp: Tell the voice how to sound, for example "calm and clear, like an audiobook narrator". Leave it empty for the natural default.
voices.tags: Tags you can write into the text: {tags}
voices.fallbackText: Reads whenever the chosen engine cannot deliver a sentence.
detect.title: Language detection
detect.text: Used when a shortcut reads with automatic language.
detect.sentence: Sentence by sentence, for mixed texts
edge.refreshed: Edge voice list is up to date.
el.keyHelp: An API key is a password that lets this app use your ElevenLabs account. It stays on this PC.
el.checking: Checking the key and its permissions…
el.noKey: No API key connected yet. Setting one up takes about a minute.
el.noTts: The key works but may not create speech, so ElevenLabs cannot read. Piper reads in the meantime.
el.noVoices: The key works but may not read the voices. Without the voice list there is nothing to choose from.
el.connectedBalance: Connected. Plan {tier}: {left} of {limit} credits left, enough for about {hours} hours with {model}.
el.connectedNoBalance: Connected. The balance shows up once the key may read "User".
el.permsFix: On the key page, edit the key (pencil icon) and set these permissions under "Restrict Key", then check again here:
el.permsOptional: Everything needed is allowed. For prices and your balance, you can also allow these on the key page:
el.step2: While creating it, turn on "Restrict Key" and set these permissions
el.step2Note: Leave everything else on "No Access". An unrestricted key works too, but is riskier if it ever gets into the wrong hands.
el.step3: Copy the key; this window picks it up by itself
el.voiceText: ElevenLabs voices speak every language. Find more in the Voice Library on elevenlabs.io: add them to "My Voices", then reload here.
el.voicesEmpty: Voices appear once the key may read them
el.retiringLong: ElevenLabs switches this standard voice off at the end of 2026, so pick another one.
el.modelText: Billed per character. One hour of reading is roughly {chars} characters.
el.creditsHelp: Credits are ElevenLabs' currency. Every character read costs credits; faster models cost half.
el.cacheText: Hearing them again is free and starts instantly.
el.speedNote: ElevenLabs reads at most 1.2 times faster; v4 and v3 have no speed setting at all.
el.activated: ElevenLabs is active. Select some text and press your shortcut.
el.perm.models: shows the real price of each model
el.model.eleven_flash_v2_5: Half price, first sound after about 75 ms. Natural, a little more even than v4. Best value.
el.model.eleven_v4: The liveliest model, as in ElevenReader. Double price, no speed control.
el.model.eleven_multilingual_v2: Calm and very steady narrator for long texts. Double price, speed adjustable.
el.model.eleven_v3: Predecessor of v4, very expressive but restless on short sentences. v4 is the better pick.
el.err.quota: Out of credits for this month.
el.err.invalidKey: The API key is not valid.
el.err.missingPerm: The API key is missing a permission: {detail}
el.err.unauthorized: The API key is not valid or lacks a permission.
el.err.rateLimit: Too many requests at once (limit of your plan).
page.speed.title: Speed & pauses
page.speed.text: Move a slider right to read faster. Listen plays a sample with the chosen engine.
speed.title: Speed
speed.help: 1.00× is the voice's natural pace. Further right reads faster: 1.25× is a quarter faster, 0.80× a fifth slower.
pause.title: Pause between sentences
pause.text: Extra silence after each sentence, for every engine. 0 turns it off.
pause.label: Pause
page.filters.title: Text clean-up
page.hotkeys.title: Shortcuts
page.hotkeys.textWin: Click a field and press the key combination. Delete or Esc clears it. Shortcuts take effect once the window is closed after saving.
page.hotkeys.textLinux: Click a field and press the key combination. Delete or Esc clears it. AltGr keys and mouse side buttons keep working through keyd.
hotkeys.title: Keyboard shortcuts
hotkey.de-ocr: Read a screen area in German
hotkey.en-ocr: Read a screen area in English
save.elNoKey: Saved. ElevenLabs still needs an API key; until then Piper reads.
save.doneOnClose: Saved. Shortcuts take effect when you close this window.
test.elNoKey: Set up the API key first, then the voices appear.
test.daemonStarting: The reading service was not running and is starting. Try again in a moment.
test.needsNvidia: {name} needs an NVIDIA graphics card. On this PC it would be too slow.
test.overBudget: {name} needs about {need} GB of graphics memory; the safe limit is {budget} GB.
test.loading: {name} is loading. The first sentence arrives in about 20 seconds.
voice.newText: One person, 10 to 15 seconds, calm and without music or echo. Only use voices you are allowed to use. The model copies noise and room sound too, so a clean recording pays off.
voice.name: Name
voice.noDevice: No device found. Check that a microphone or speaker is connected.
voice.pcHint: Records whatever plays on this output, for example a video. Start the recording first, then press play.
voice.micHint: Speak at a normal volume about a hand's width from the microphone. Reading a short text aloud works best.
voice.resultBad: This recording does not work as a voice.
voice.savedUsed: Voice "{name}" is saved and in use. Try it with Listen.
voice.savedListed: Voice "{name}" is saved and waiting in the voice list.
manage.text: These recordings are what the voices are cloned from. Deleting one is permanent; if it was in use, the standard voice takes over.
manage.emptyTitle: No voices of your own yet
manage.emptyText: Record 10 to 15 seconds or pick an audio file, and the model reads with that voice.
voices.check.tooShort: Only {s} s of speech. Record 10 to 15 s for a good clone.
voices.check.short: {s} s of speech, that works. 10 to 15 s usually sound steadier.
voices.check.clipped: The recording is too loud and may crackle. Record a little quieter.
voices.check.quiet: Very quiet. Move closer to the microphone or play it louder.
voices.check.noisy: Lots of background noise (only {db} dB apart). Record somewhere quieter, or the model copies the noise.
voices.err.noFfmpeg: ffmpeg is missing; without it only WAV files work
voices.err.wav16: Without ffmpeg only 16-bit WAV files can be read
onb.welcome.title: Hi! I'll read to you.
onb.welcome.text: Select text in any app, press a shortcut, and listen. Great for long articles, tired eyes, or learning a language.
onb.welcome.howtoNoKey: You pick a shortcut for reading at the end.
onb.welcome.time: Takes about a minute. Everything can be changed later.
onb.engine.title: Who should read to you?
onb.engine.text: We took a quick look at your PC and picked what runs best on it.
onb.engine.usesVram: Uses about {gb} GB of graphics memory.
onb.engine.elevenlabs: Prefer premium cloud voices? ElevenLabs can be connected any time in the settings.
onb.hw.vramHelp: Big voice models run on an NVIDIA graphics card and use its memory (VRAM). The app only ever uses a safe share, so games and videos keep running smoothly.
onb.hw.cpuPath: Voices run on the processor, which works well for Kokoro and the online voices.
onb.install.title: More voices you can add
onb.install.text: These run on your PC once installed. Copy the command, paste it into a terminal, and reopen this window when it is done.
onb.install.needsNvidia: Needs an NVIDIA graphics card with about {gb} GB of free memory.
onb.install.notHere: This PC has no NVIDIA card, so it would not run here.
onb.install.noScript: There is no installer for this system yet.
onb.install.copied: Command copied. Paste it into a terminal (PowerShell or Terminal) to install.
onb.voice.title: Pick a voice you like
onb.voice.text: Tap Listen to hear each one. You can switch any time.
onb.voice.auto: This engine picks a fitting voice by itself.
onb.speed.title: How fast should I read?
onb.speed.text: Pick a pace that feels comfortable. Listen plays a short sample.
onb.speed.fast: Need it faster now and then? Use
onb.clone.title: Want it to sound like someone you know?
onb.clone.text: {engine} can read with any voice. Record 10 to 15 seconds or pick an audio file, and it sounds like that person.
onb.clone.consent: Only use voices you are allowed to use, like your own.
onb.done.title: You're all set!
onb.done.text: Select text in any app and press
onb.done.textNoKey: Pick your shortcuts in the settings under Shortcuts.
onb.done.change: Shortcuts, voices and speed can be changed in the settings whenever you like.
onb.welcomeToSettings: Here is everything you can adjust. Changes apply with Save and apply.
tray.fallback: Switch to Piper when the engine fails
follow.title: Follow along
follow.setting: Shows the text in a small window while it is read and marks the word you hear.
tray.readerSend: Listen to the selection in ElevenReader
tray.msg.nothingSelected: Nothing selected. Select some text (or copy it with Ctrl+C) and press the shortcut.
tray.msg.readerNothing: Nothing selected. Select some text and press the shortcut.
tray.msg.readerConnectText: One time only: a guide has opened in your browser. Afterwards your text is handed over automatically.
tray.msg.readerConnected: Signed in as {email}. Ctrl+Alt+E sends selected text straight to ElevenReader.
tray.msg.readerFallback: {error} The text is read locally instead.
tray.msg.ocrMissing: Text recognition (tesseract) is not installed. Install it with: winget install UB-Mannheim.TesseractOCR
tray.msg.daemonDown: The reading service was not reachable and is starting. Please try again.
tray.msg.alreadyRunning: Recito TTS is already running; this second copy closes.
rules.undone: Your rules are back to how they were before the last change.
rules.emptyText: A rule tells the voice how to say something, for example "SQL" as "S Q L" or "z.B." as "zum Beispiel".
rules.kind.word.desc: Finds the text only where it stands on its own, so "SQL" leaves "MySQL" alone.
rules.kind.literal.desc: Finds the text exactly as written, also inside longer words.
rules.kind.regex.desc: For advanced patterns. The replacement can reuse groups with \1.
rules.byAgentTip: An AI assistant added or changed this rule. Keep it, change it or delete it.
rules.toReviewOne: One rule from an AI assistant is waiting for your review.
rules.toReview: {n} rules from an AI assistant are waiting for your review.
rules.reviewText: An AI assistant suggested this rule. Keep it as it is, change it, or delete it.
rules.replacementHint: Leave it empty to skip the text.
rules.previewLabel: With the text from Try it
rules.previewNone: This rule does not change the text from Try it.
rules.tryText: Type or paste some text and see what the voice will read.
rules.trySample: The **SQL** report, e.g. for Monday, is ready.
rules.err.kind: Choose how to find the text.
rules.err.regex: This is not a valid regular expression: {detail}
rules.err.emptyMatch: This pattern also matches empty text, so it would change every spot.
rules.err.template: The replacement does not fit the pattern: {detail}
rules.err.replacement: The replacement has to be text.
rules.err.notFound: This rule no longer exists. The list is up to date again.
rules.err.store: Your rules could not be read or saved: {detail}
ai.title: Instructions for an AI assistant
ai.text: Coding assistants such as Claude Code or Codex can manage your rules with a small command line tool. Paste these instructions into the assistant's chat. Rules it adds appear here for your review.
ai.copied: Instructions copied. Paste them into your AI assistant.
beta.reader: Uses an unofficial ElevenReader interface and may stop working at any time.
onb.el.cost: ElevenLabs bills per character read. The free plan includes 10,000 credits every month, enough for about {minutes} minutes with {model}. For more, you need a paid plan.
onb.el.keyText: Create an API key on the ElevenLabs website and paste it here. The key stays on this PC.
onb.el.permHint: If you restrict the key, allow "Text to Speech" and "Voices".
onb.el.saved: A key is already saved on this PC. Check it to load your voices.
onb.el.needKey: Check your key to continue with ElevenLabs, or pick another option above.
onb.keys.title: Your shortcuts
onb.keys.text: These keys work in every app. Keep the suggestions or click a field and press a new combination.
onb.keys.hint: Delete or Esc clears a field. Use Ctrl or Alt in each combination, so normal typing never triggers it.
onb.keys.dup: Already used for "{action}". Pick another combination.
onb.keys.noModifier: Add Ctrl or Alt, otherwise normal typing would trigger it.
onb.keys.taken: Another program already uses this combination.
onb.keys.fixFirst: Fix the marked shortcuts to continue, or skip this step.
onb.welcome.sample: Hi! This is how I read your text aloud.
onb.welcome.triedMore: Works like this in every app.
lang.title: Languages you read
lang.text: Pick every language your texts are in. Language detection only chooses among these, and each one gets its own voice.
lang.gap.engine: This language is not available with {engine}.
lang.gap.piperNone: No Piper voice for this language yet.
lang.gap.byEdge: The Edge voice {voice} reads it, online.
lang.gap.byEngine: The chosen engine reads it. A Piper voice only steps in if that fails.
lang.gap.none: Nothing can read it yet. Download a Piper voice for it.
onb.langs.title: Which languages do you read?
onb.langs.text: Pick every language your texts are in. I recognize the language of each text and use the right voice.
onb.langs.hint: Next you choose who reads. If an engine does not speak one of your languages, Piper or Edge reads it.
page.rules.text: Before a text is read aloud, it runs through the rules below, from top to bottom. The first groups come with the app: they remove Markdown and Obsidian marks and turn formulas into words. Change them, switch them off, or add your own rules at the end.
rules.title: Rules
rules.text: A rule finds a piece of text and says what the voice reads instead. Changes apply to the next text you read.
rules.group.obsidian.desc: Removes Obsidian syntax: links such as [[Page|Name]], embeds, tags, callouts, comments and highlights.
rules.group.markdown.desc: Removes Markdown marks such as **, # and table lines, shortens web addresses and reads formulas between $ signs.
rules.group.formulas.desc: Reads copied LaTeX and math symbols as words, for example from Readest. Formulas are read in German.
rules.group.user.desc: Your own rules run last, on the text the groups above have tidied up.
rules.missing: {n} rules of this group were deleted.
rules.missingOne: One rule of this group was deleted.
rules.restoredNone: The presets are already as they came with the app.
rules.groupRestored: The {group} rules are back and switched on.
rules.resetDone: The rule is back to how it came with the app.
rules.changedTip: You changed this rule. Reset to original brings back how it came with the app.
rules.codeTip: This rule runs program code, so there is no pattern to edit. You can switch it on or off, move it or delete it.
rules.presetText: This rule comes with the app: {name}. Change it as you like. Reset to original brings back how it came.
rules.err.builtin: This code rule is not available: {detail}
rules.err.codeFixed: Built-in rules have no pattern to edit. You can switch them on or off.
rules.err.notPreset: This rule did not come with the app, so there is no original to go back to.
preset.md-front-matter: Skip the properties at the top
preset.dollar-math.desc: Turns $x^2$ into words such as "x hoch zwei". Formulas are read in German.
preset.md-url: Web addresses: read only the site name
preset.md-table-cells: Tables: a short pause between cells
preset.md-table-edges: Tables: skip the | at both ends of a row
preset.latex.desc: Turns copied formulas, for example from Readest, into German words.
